basics.name: Royce Cornwell
basics.label: Software Engineer
basics.summary: Software engineer focused on backend, full-stack, and event-driven development, currently completing an M.Sc. in Computer Science in Berlin. I build and ship features across the database, backend, and UI layers, scope ambiguous problems end-to-end, and place a strong emphasis on reliable, well-tested, and clearly documented software.

education.institution: International University of Applied Science, Berlin, Germany

work.summary: Software engineering intern at Doctolib, working full-stack on e-prescription with the Clinical team and full-stack on patient intake with the Practice Operations team.
highlights: Owned technical scoping for an e-prescription print-layout migration end-to-end: reproduced current behavior, reconciled conflicting design and specification sources, and produced a complete, engineering-ready backlog with acceptance criteria

Investigated a data-access issue that locked practitioners out of prescriptions after patient-record merges — traced the root cause through the Ruby on Rails monolith and shipped a safe, batched background migration to remove the underlying schema dependency
Shipped full-stack features across TypeScript and Kotlin, including a new user-facing display and a new field threaded through the front end, backend, and PDF templating layer

Delivered independent backend work with the Practice Operations team on an unfamiliar codebase (Spring Boot / Kotlin / PostgreSQL), including a database migration and domain modeling with test-driven development
Wrote developer documentation adopted by the team and diagnosed and fixed local developer-tooling issues, sharing the fix with the wider team
Validated appointment-update behavior by querying the database directly, confirming that each change correctly produced its corresponding record

work.summary: Working student building and testing scientific-instrumentation hardware for neuroscience research
highlights: Built and tested GPS trackers for hummingbird research, with supporting documentation
Helped develop PCB libraries for a neurosurgical tool used in rodent brain research (Arduino).

work.summary: Modernized safety controls for a high-powered laser system as an Akamai Workforce Initiative intern
highlights: Upgraded the safety-control system for a high-powered laser: updated PLC ladder-logic (RSLogix500) to meet safety standards, designed wire layouts, and wired Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) switches
Tested and verified PLC functionality and presented the project in a technical format

volunteer.summary: Tutored kids at the community center with homework and learning Japanese
highlights: Created a study plan for beginner Japanese learning

awards.title: JASSO Scholarship
awards.summary: The Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO) offers scholarships for qualified international students who are accepted by a Japanese university. I was accepted for one semester as an exchange student and awarded for my academic standings.

awards.title: Alakaina Scholarship
awards.awarder: University of Hawaii at Kauai Community College
awards.summary: Before transferring to a 4-year institution, I was awarded with the Alakaina foundation  for a written essay about their passion for engineering and alongside their GPA of 3.5 and above.
